Laws.heading: Laws and terms in plain words
Laws.note: Dates and summaries below are supplied for public information and must be checked against the official gazette. This is not legal advice.

items.title: Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956
items.plain: Covers Hindus, Buddhists, Jains, and Sikhs.

items.title: Guardians and Wards Act, 1890
items.plain: Provides for guardianship, not full adoption, for Muslims, Christians, Jews, and Parsis.

items.title: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
items.plain: Covers all religions. It provides for Child Welfare Committees, registration of child care institutions, and offences including illegal adoption.

items.title: Juvenile Justice Amendment Act, 2021
items.plain: The District Magistrate issues adoption orders.

items.title: Adoption Regulations, 2022
items.plain: Detailed rules for adoption through CARA.

items.title: POCSO Act, 2012
items.plain: Every person must report child sexual abuse.

items.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
items.plain: The children's data rules apply from 13 May 2027.

Care with the prospective adoptive family before the adoption order, as allowed by the official process.

Follow-up that may continue for up to two years.
A child lives with a family for a period while remaining legally connected to their birth family.
The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act.

Help.title: Help and contact
Help.intro: For urgent child-safety concerns, call Childline 1098. Growity is not an emergency service.

questions.question: Does Growity arrange adoptions?
questions.answer: No. Growity is not an adoption agency and cannot choose, refer, place, or grant an adoption. Legal adoption happens through CARINGS, recognised agencies, Child Welfare Committees, and the District Magistrate.

questions.question: Can parents browse children on this website?
questions.answer: No. Child information is shown only after an official CARINGS referral and only to the referred family and authorised staff. Child media is not shown before the adoption order is recorded.

questions.question: How do I report a child-safety concern?
questions.answer: Call Childline 1098, free 24x7. A child with a Growity account may also make a confidential report. Contact local emergency services if there is immediate danger.

questions.question: Who can see a child's complaint?
questions.answer: Only authorised protection staff assigned or on call for the complaint. NGO staff, foster families, accused people, and other staff cannot see it.

questions.question: Can I get legal advice here?
questions.answer: No. Growity shares general information only. Please contact a qualified legal professional or the relevant public authority.

questions.question: How can I request my data?
questions.answer: Adults who have left care may view or download their own data and ask staff to delete non-legally-required information. Some minimal legal records must be retained for a period still to be set by a lawyer.

Help.contactBody: For account access, records, or general questions, contact the Growity team using the address provided by your local programme. Do not send child complaint details or documents by ordinary email.

titles.staff-code: Staff Code of Conduct and Confidentiality Agreement

Policies.terms: Use Growity only through an account authorised for you. Keep your sign-in details private and submit accurate information. Do not seek private adoption arrangements, browse children, or share another person’s records. Official adoption decisions are made by the authorities responsible under law.
Policies.privacy: Growity uses information to provide the service requested. Access is separated by role and assigned work; private documents are stored in restricted storage, and sensitive access is logged. You may request a copy of your own data and request deletion where allowed. Some records may have to be retained under law. Growity does not publish children’s private records or use them for advertising.
Policies.child-safety: If a child is in immediate danger, call Childline 1098 or local emergency services. Reports in Growity are for authorised protection staff who need to respond. Growity is not an emergency service and does not replace legal reporting duties. Volunteers, NGOs, foster families, and people named in a report cannot read a child’s confidential complaint.
Policies.parent-terms: Parent users must submit true documents, consent to checks and home visits required by the official process, and use CARINGS and public authorities for adoption. No private adoption or child browsing is permitted through Growity.
Policies.ngo-terms: NGOs must provide accurate information, record a CWC order number for every child entry, keep recognition and compliance records current, follow funding rules, and cooperate with audits. NGO staff cannot access children's complaints.
Policies.staff-code: Staff must protect confidential information, access only assigned cases, document relevant actions, preserve complaint confidentiality, and report corruption, harassment, or inconvenience through the grievance process. Administrators do not receive complaint or grievance access by default.
Policies.complaints: Child complaints are visible only to assigned or on-call protection officers. Emergency reports require prompt action, a 24-hour outcome record, and a record of who was contacted, when, and how. Staff grievances are available only to the grievance committee.
Policies.retention: Adults who have left care can access and download their own data and request deletion of non-legally-required data for staff review. Minimal legal records remain locked for a period to be set by a lawyer, and are read only following a logged written legal request. Children's data requires verifiable guardian consent.
Policies.cookies: Growity uses authentication cookies and essential session storage when secure account features are connected. Do not use optional tracking or advertising cookies in the child-safety areas.
Policies.disclaimer: Growity is not an adoption agency, does not choose or place a child, does not grant an adoption, and does not provide legal advice. Legal adoption happens only through CARA's CARINGS portal, recognised Specialised Adoption Agencies, Child Welfare Committees, and the District Magistrate. Verify legal dates with the official gazette.
Policies.publicNotice: Plain-language information about this website. It is not legal advice or an official adoption decision.

Volunteering.title: Volunteering with verified partners
Volunteering.intro: Universities and registered organisations can ask about supervised community activities hosted with verified partners. Volunteering never gives access to a child’s case, documents, contact details, or private reports.
Volunteering.eligibility: A coordinator from a registered university or organisation should contact a verified NGO or the Growity Team. The host must confirm the organisation, volunteer screening, training, and safeguarding plan before any activity involving children is approved.
activities: Group games, arts, reading, and age-appropriate entertainment with host staff present.
Structured mentoring or learning sessions approved by the host and delivered with trained adult supervision.
Cleaning drives and community-care activities on host premises, without access to private records or child contact details.
Other group social activities for young people after the verified host approves the plan.
safeguards: Child-facing activity requires a verified host, identity/background checks, safeguarding orientation, and continuous host supervision.
No unsupervised or private one-to-one contact, private messaging, photography, or sharing a child’s story.
Volunteers never see children’s records, complaint details, case status, or contact information.
A child can decline to participate. Report any concern to the host protection lead or call 1098 for urgent help.
Volunteering.recognition: Recognition depends on attendance confirmed by the verified host and its written rules. Participation points and certificates are not guaranteed; Growity does not currently calculate points or issue certificates or academic credit.
Volunteering.academicNote: Only your university or course authority can decide whether any activity counts toward a degree. Confirm its written rules before volunteering; Growity cannot guarantee or award academic credit.
Volunteering.next: Ask your university or registered organisation to nominate a coordinator, then contact a verified NGO or the Growity Team. Do not visit a child-care site or contact a child unless the verified host has approved and scheduled the activity.
